q: Which of these is not a sequence?
why: A sequence is ordered and indexable by position. A set is neither, which is why `s[0]` raises.
`x[-1]` is `x[len(x) - 1]` computed for you, so it fails on an empty sequence exactly as `x[0]` does.
Slices clamp their bounds to what exists. Indexing raises when you are wrong; slicing quietly gives you less.
The stop is exclusive, which is why `x[:n] + x[n:]` reconstructs the original for any `n`.

options: Reverses in place and returns None
why: `x.reverse()` mutates and returns `None`; `reversed(x)` gives an iterator and copies nothing.
Every in-place operation in the standard library returns `None`, so chaining off one fails immediately instead of quietly.

q: `items[:] = other` differs from `items = other` in that
options: It replaces the contents of the existing list, so every name bound to it sees the change
why: Slice assignment targets the object; plain assignment rebinds a name. Unit 02's distinction in slicing form.

options: Works, and the list gets shorter
why: Slice assignment can change the length. An extended slice, one with a step, is stricter and demands an exact match.

q: For a tuple `t`, `t[:] is t` is
why: Copying an immutable value would achieve nothing, so the original comes back. For a list it is a new object.
`range` implements the whole sequence interface with arithmetic and stores nothing, which is why wrapping it in `list` is usually a habit worth dropping.

q: `out += name` where `out` is a list and `name` is `"ada"` gives
why: `+=` on a list is `extend`, which walks whatever it is given, and walking a string yields characters. `append` adds one element.

why: The stop is exclusive and `len(values)` is already one past the last index. `values[1:-1]` is the one that drops both ends.

q: `first, *rest = row` differs from `row[0], row[1:]` in that
options: It raises ValueError when the shape is wrong, instead of returning something plausible
why: Slicing is forgiving, which is right when a short result is a reasonable answer. Unpacking is strict, which is right when the shape is part of the contract.
